name: SimplePractice vs Jane App
title: SimplePractice vs Jane App: EHR Comparison for Therapists (2026)
description: Compare SimplePractice and Jane App - two popular practice management platforms. See differences in pricing, telehealth, insurance billing, mobile apps, and which is best for your therapy practice.

summary.bottom_line: SimplePractice is purpose-built for mental health with stronger insurance billing and telehealth, while Jane App excels at complex scheduling for multidisciplinary clinics. Solo therapists typically prefer SimplePractice; integrative practices with multiple disciplines lean toward Jane.

sections.heading: SimplePractice vs Jane App: Overview
sections.content: SimplePractice and Jane App are both popular practice management platforms, but they serve different primary audiences. SimplePractice was built specifically for mental health professionals—therapists, counselors, and social workers—with deep insurance billing integration and robust telehealth. Jane App originated in the allied health space (physical therapy, chiropractic, massage) and excels at complex scheduling scenarios involving multiple practitioners, rooms, and equipment. Both are HIPAA-compliant and offer core EHR functionality.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: SimplePractice starts at $49/month (Starter), $79/month (Essential), and $99/month (Plus). Jane App starts at $54/month with pricing that scales based on practice size. A key difference: Jane includes unlimited file storage and free admin accounts on all plans, while SimplePractice charges for additional clinician seats ($74/each) and reserves some features for higher tiers. For solo therapists, SimplePractice's Starter plan is more affordable; for practices with admin staff, Jane's free admin seats can offset its higher base price.

sections.heading: Feature Comparison
sections.content: The biggest differentiator is insurance billing: SimplePractice has built-in claims submission through Change Healthcare at $0.25/claim, while Jane requires a separate clearinghouse add-on. For telehealth, SimplePractice supports group sessions with up to 15 participants; Jane's telehealth is limited to 1:1 sessions. SimplePractice offers e-prescribing as an add-on ($49/mo), which Jane does not support. However, Jane's scheduling system is widely considered superior for complex multi-practitioner, multi-room coordination—Capterra reviewers consistently praise it as the best in class for busy appointment-driven clinics.

sections.heading: Mobile Experience
sections.content: SimplePractice has a clear advantage with native iOS and Android apps for scheduling, notes, and client messaging on the go. Jane App has no native mobile app—access is through a responsive mobile web browser. For practitioners who run their day from a phone, SimplePractice is the better choice.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your practice type and billing needs:

recommendations.when: You're a mental health professional who bills insurance, needs e-prescribing, wants robust telehealth with group sessions, or prefers a native mobile app
You run a multidisciplinary clinic (PT, chiro, nutrition + therapy), need complex multi-room/multi-provider scheduling, or have multiple admin staff (free admin accounts)
You're a solo cash-pay therapist with straightforward scheduling needs—both will serve you well

faqs.q: Is SimplePractice or Jane App better for solo therapists?
faqs.a: For solo mental health therapists, SimplePractice is generally the better fit. It's purpose-built for behavioral health with integrated insurance billing, more robust telehealth (including group sessions), and a native mobile app. Jane App's strengths in complex scheduling are less relevant for solo practitioners.

faqs.q: Does Jane App have insurance billing like SimplePractice?
faqs.a: Jane App supports billing workflows, but insurance claim submission requires a separate paid clearinghouse add-on. SimplePractice has built-in insurance claims through Change Healthcare at $0.25 per claim, making it more streamlined for insurance-based practices.

faqs.q: Which has better telehealth: SimplePractice or Jane?
faqs.a: SimplePractice has more robust telehealth, supporting both individual and group sessions with up to 15 participants, plus automated appointment reminders. Jane's telehealth is limited to 1:1 sessions. Both are HIPAA-compliant.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Jane App to SimplePractice?
faqs.a: Yes, both platforms support data migration. You'll need to export your data from Jane and work with SimplePractice support for import. Plan for 2-4 weeks to fully transition, and consider running both systems in parallel during the migration.
